Model Methodology — Jamestown Analytics Framework

Waltzing Analytics application of Jamestown Analytics · Marc Lamberts, FC Hradec Králové · built on Brighton & Hove Albion, Hearts & St. Gilloise
Methodology: Jamestown Analytics
Applied by: Marc Lamberts · Waltzing Analytics
Club: FC Hradec Králové
Built on: Brighton · Hearts · St. Gilloise
Data: Wyscout per-90 · Impect API

The Jamestown Analytics Edge — Why This Works

Core insight: Market values in lower leagues are driven by reputation, agent relationships, and past narratives — NOT objective statistical output. Jamestown Analytics exploits this gap systematically.

Jamestown Analytics is the methodology — developed and refined through three clubs that proved data-driven recruitment works at every level: Brighton & Hove Albion, Heart of Midlothian (Hearts), and St. Gilloise. Marc Lamberts applies this framework through Waltzing Analytics for FC Hradec Králové.

The approach requires ignoring reputation, ignoring league prestige bias, and trusting the numbers when they conflict with conventional wisdom. Jamestown proved this works across multiple leagues and countries — Waltzing Analytics now applies the same logic to the Czech and Slovak pyramid.

Statistical Quality Score (SQS)

The SQS is a position-weighted composite of Wyscout per-90 metrics, normalised to a 0–100 percentile scale within each position group and recruitment league pool.

SQS = Σ (metric × weight) × league_difficulty_coefficient

Each position group has a bespoke weight matrix prioritising the metrics that most predict success at that position. A striker's SQS weights finishing and box presence heavily; a DM's SQS weights defensive actions and ball progression.

PositionPrimary metricsKey weights
GKSave rate, Prevented goals×3.5, ×3.0
CBDef duels won%, Aerial%, Interceptions×3.0, ×2.5, ×2.5
FBProg runs, xA, Def duels×2.5, ×2.5, ×2.0
DMInterceptions, Def duels, Prog passes×3.0, ×2.5, ×2.0
CMProg passes, Key passes, xG+xA×2.5, ×2.5, ×2.0
WGoals, xG, Dribbles, Box touches×3.5, ×3.0, ×2.0
FWGoals, xG, Box touches, Aerial%×3.5, ×3.0, ×2.5

Lamberts Index (LI)

The Lamberts Index quantifies the gap between a player's statistical output rank and their market price rank. It is the core "edge" metric.

LI = SQS Percentile Rank − Market Value Percentile Rank

Range: −100 to +100. A positive LI means the player's statistical output exceeds their price in the market — they are underpriced. A negative LI means the market overcharges relative to output.

ELITE VALUE ≥30 Priced ≥30 percentile ranks below statistical output. Strong buy signal.
HIGH VALUE ≥20 Significant undervaluation. High priority for scouting visit.
VALUE ≥10 Moderate undervaluation. Worth monitoring and assessing further.
FAIR PRICE 0–9 Priced in line with statistical output. No clear edge.
OVERVALUED <0 Market overcharges relative to output. Avoid unless non-statistical value.

League Difficulty Adjustment

Stats produced in stronger leagues count more. Stats produced in stronger leagues count more. We apply difficulty multipliers before computing SQS.

LeagueCoefficientRationale
CZ×0.90Czech First League, top professional standard
CZ II×0.82Second tier Czech, professional standard
Slovakia×0.78Slovak top flight, competitive
CZ U19×0.65Czech U19 elite, high-potential youth pool

This means a player in CZ (top flight) with a raw SQS of 80 ranks higher than an equivalent CZ II player, who in turn ranks higher than a Slovakia or CZ U19 player — correctly reflecting the relative competition levels.

Jamestown Analytics — Three-Club Foundation

Jamestown Analytics is built on lessons from three clubs that each proved a different dimension of data-driven recruitment:

Brighton The edge metric: SQS percentile rank vs. market value percentile rank = the Lamberts Index. Find players statistically priced below their output. Proved across Championship → Premier League.
Hearts The validation layer: Event-data packing scores (Impect) as a second, independent signal. Both Wyscout AND Impect must agree before a player reaches Priority 1 — reduces false positives.
St. Gilloise The market lens: Target structurally inefficient mid-tier leagues where statistical talent is systematically underpriced. CZ II and Slovakia offer the same arbitrage Belgium's Pro League once did.

Waltzing Analytics applies the full Jamestown framework — Brighton edge-finding + Hearts dual validation + St. Gilloise market targeting — to the Czech and Slovak football pyramid for FC Hradec Králové.

vs Hradec Gap — Upgrade Quantification

The vs Hradec gap answers the question: "By how much does this candidate exceed our current starters?" We take the two Hradec players with the most minutes at each position (from Impect tracking data), average their quality percentile score, and subtract it from the candidate's SQS rank. A gap of +25 means the candidate is at the 25th percentile better than the current starter — a meaningful, quantified upgrade.

CLEAR UPGRADE
SQS gap ≥ +10 above current starter average. Immediate first-team improvement.
ROTATIONAL / COVER
Near-equivalent quality. Provides competition and depth without clear step up.
DEPTH
Below current starter level. Squad depth only. Rarely recommended under budget constraint.

Scouting Uncertainty — Confidence in the Numbers

Core insight: The Lamberts Index and SQS are only as trustworthy as the data behind them. A high LI built on 400 minutes and one unconfirmed data source is a lead, not a conclusion — Scouting Uncertainty makes that distinction explicit instead of hiding it inside a single ranking number.

Every candidate gets an uncertainty score (0–100, higher = less confidence) built from three factors, shown wherever the candidate appears in the workbook and broken down in full on their Player Profile.

FactorPenaltyRationale
Sample size+42 if <900 mins · +20 if 900–1,800 mins · +0 if ≥1,800 minsPer-90 rates swing wildly on small samples — early-season or fringe players can post flattering or misleading numbers.
Source confirmation+38 no Impect data · +18 Impect present but doesn't confirm · +0 dual-signalHearts' validation layer: a signal only Wyscout sees is weaker evidence than two independent data sources agreeing.
League translation risk+0 CZ · +6 CZ II · +9 Slovakia · +16 CZ U19Output produced further from the target level (CZ I) carries more risk in projecting forward to senior first-team football.
LOW (score ≤ 20)
Large sample, dual-signal confirmed, top-flight data. Trust the number.
MEDIUM (score 21–50)
One weak factor — moderate sample, single source, or lower-tier league. Verify before acting.
HIGH (score > 50)
Multiple weak factors compound — small sample, unconfirmed, and/or youth football. Scout in person before committing budget.

Waltzing Analytics — The Model

Marc Lamberts · FC Hradec Králové 2025–26 · One integrated model, four pillars
By: Marc Lamberts
Brand: Waltzing Analytics
Club: FC Hradec Králové
Inspired by: Jamestown Analytics (Brighton, Hearts, St. Gilloise)
What is Waltzing Analytics?

One integrated recruitment model that finds statistically undervalued players, validates the signal through event-data packing scores, targets the right markets, and quantifies the upgrade over current starters.

Developed by Marc Lamberts for FC Hradec Králové. Inspired by Jamestown Analytics methodology (Brighton & Hove Albion, Hearts, St. Gilloise).

1
Statistical Quality Score (SQS)
Wyscout per-90 · position-weighted · league-adjusted

Every player gets a position-specific composite score built from their Wyscout per-90 statistics, weighted by what matters most at each position — finishing for forwards, defensive duels for centre-backs, progressive passing for midfielders.

SQS = Σ (metric × weight) × league_coefficient

League coefficients (CZ 0.90 · CZ II 0.82 · Slovakia 0.78 · U19 0.65) ensure a CZ player scoring 80 raw ranks higher than a CZ II equivalent — correctly reflecting competition level. The final SQS is a 0–100 percentile rank within each position group across all four leagues.

Where you see it: SQS column · Value Map · By Position · Lamberts Model chart
2
Lamberts Index (LI)
The edge metric · output rank vs. price rank

The core insight: market values in lower leagues are driven by narrative, not output. The Lamberts Index measures the gap between what a player produces statistically and what the market charges for them.

LI = SQS Percentile Rank − Market Value Percentile Rank

Positive LI = player produces more than they cost. LI ≥ 30 = Elite Value — strong buy signal. LI ≥ 20 = High Value. The higher the LI, the bigger the market inefficiency being exploited.

Where you see it: LI column · Value Tier (Elite/High/Value/Fair/Over) · Value Map · all ranking sorts
3
Impect Dual Validation
Event-data packing scores · independent second signal

Wyscout per-90 stats can be inflated by playing style, team context, or small samples. Impect packing scores measure something different — how many opponents a player bypasses with the ball. Two independent data sources that independently agree = high confidence.

●● Dual Signal = Wyscout SQS ≥ 60 AND Impect ≥ 60
◆ Impect Gem = Impect ≥ 60, SQS < 60 (hidden value)

Dual-signal players reach Priority 1 in the Recommendations tab. Gems are flagged for manual scouting. Conviction Score = avg(SQS, Impect percentile) — the single best number for ranking recommendations.

Where you see it: Impect tab · Signal column · Recommendations · Conviction score
4
vs Hradec Gap
Upgrade quantification · position-specific baseline

Finding an undervalued player is only useful if they're actually better than what we already have. The vs Hradec gap measures exactly that — how much a candidate exceeds the current Hradec starter at their position.

Gap = Player SQS − avg(top-2 HK starters at position)

Gap ≥ +10 = Clear Upgrade — immediate first-team improvement. Near-zero = Rotational. Negative = Depth only. The gap is calculated from Impect tracking data for Hradec's actual 2025-26 squad at each position.

Where you see it: vs HK column · Clear Upgrades tab · Squad Baseline · Exec Summary

How the Model Works — From Raw Data to Recommendation

①
Input
Wyscout per-90 stats + Impect packing scores for all players in CZ, CZ II, Slovakia, CZ U19
②
Score
Compute SQS (Pillar 1) per position. Apply league difficulty. Rank across all four leagues.
③
Edge
Calculate Lamberts Index (Pillar 2) — SQS rank minus market value rank. Tier the market inefficiency.
④
Validate
Cross-reference Impect (Pillar 3). Flag Dual Signal and Gems. Compute Conviction Score.
⑤
Recommend
Apply HK gap (Pillar 4). P1 = Dual + Clear Upgrade. P2 = Dual + Rotational. Watch = Gem.
Inspiration: The Waltzing Analytics model draws on the Jamestown Analytics philosophy — pioneered through work at Brighton & Hove Albion (the statistical edge-finding approach), Heart of Midlothian (event-data dual validation), and Royale Union St. Gilloise (mid-tier market targeting). These clubs proved the principles work. This model applies them as one integrated system for the Czech and Slovak football pyramid.
